nodes.name: contract
nodes.task: Create contracts/retry-policy.md as the authoritative retry specification shared by the TypeScript and Python SDK clients (repository-relative paths; this is the repo root). First inspect clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py, plus any adjacent SDK helpers/config, to learn the existing request paths, HTTP libraries, error types, timeout/config surface and public API conventions, so the contract is expressible against the code that exists rather than an invented one. Then write the spec so both SDKs must implement identical policy semantics, covering at minimum: retryable HTTP statuses (429 and 503) as the defined retry set; Retry-After header handling (delta-seconds and HTTP-date forms, clock-skew/clamping rules, precedence over backoff); exponential backoff with a clearly defined base delay, multiplier, growth cap, and whether/how jitter is applied; maximum attempts (total tries vs retries, a stated default, and a config override name); and non-idempotent request protection (which methods/operations are automatically retried, how a caller marks a request safe, and the default when the safety signal is absent). Also specify non-retryable statuses, transport/network errors, attempt exhaustion, the shape of the error surfaced to callers, and explicitly list what is out of scope (no retry logic in the server or browser app). Choices the request leaves open (exact delay values, default attempt count, jitter strategy, safety-signal mechanism) must be resolved by you and recorded unambiguously with numeric values and rationale, because both implementations treat this document as binding. Verify the document is internally consistent and that every behavior an implementer needs is pinned down. Completion criterion: contracts/retry-policy.md exists and defines the retry set, Retry-After rules, backoff formula and parameters, attempt limits, idempotence gating and exhaustion/error behavior without requiring further clarification.

nodes.name: implement-typescript
nodes.task: Implement the retry policy for the TypeScript SDK client in clients/typescript/client.ts, together with unit tests for it, exactly as specified by contracts/retry-policy.md (repository-relative paths; this is the repo root). Read contracts/retry-policy.md first and treat it as the binding contract; read the existing client to follow its current request path, error types, config/option surface and code conventions. Cover every clause the contract assigns to a client: the retryable status set (429 and 503), Retry-After handling including both header forms and clamping/precedence, the exponential backoff formula with its base/multiplier/cap and jitter rule, the attempt limit with its default and config override, non-idempotent request protection including the safety signal and the default when it is absent, plus non-retryable status, transport-error and exhaustion behavior and the surfaced error shape. Where the contract pins a value, use that value rather than inventing your own; if a detail is genuinely missing or contradictory, choose the minimal interpretation consistent with the contract and record the ambiguity plus your decision in your final summary. Write unit tests using the test framework already present in the repository (inspect for an existing test directory/config instead of assuming one) that exercise the policy deterministically — for example by injecting a clock/sleep and a fake transport so tests do not wait on real delays — covering: retry on 429 and 503, no retry on other 4xx/5xx, Retry-After honored for delta-seconds and HTTP-date, backoff growth and cap, stop at maximum attempts with the specified error, non-idempotent requests not retried, and explicit opt-in making them retryable. Keep all changes confined to the TypeScript SDK client and its tests; do not add retry behavior to the server or the browser app, and do not modify contracts/retry-policy.md or clients/python. Run the unit tests you added and make them pass. Completion criterion: clients/typescript/client.ts implements the contract, unit tests for the behaviors above exist in the TypeScript test area, and the test run reports them passing.

nodes.name: implement-python
nodes.task: Implement the retry policy for the Python SDK client in clients/python/client.py, together with unit tests for it, exactly as specified by contracts/retry-policy.md (repository-relative paths; this is the repo root). Read contracts/retry-policy.md first and treat it as the binding contract; read the existing client to follow its current request path, exception types, config/option surface and code conventions. Cover every clause the contract assigns to a client: the retryable status set (429 and 503), Retry-After handling including both header forms and clamping/precedence, the exponential backoff formula with its base/multiplier/cap and jitter rule, the attempt limit with its default and config override, non-idempotent request protection including the safety signal and the default when it is absent, plus non-retryable status, transport-error and exhaustion behavior and the surfaced error shape. Where the contract pins a value, use that value rather than inventing your own; if a detail is genuinely missing or contradictory, choose the minimal interpretation consistent with the contract and record the ambiguity plus your decision in your final summary. Write unit tests using the test framework already present in the Python package (inspect for an existing test directory/config, e.g. pytest conventions, instead of assuming one) that exercise the policy deterministically — for example by monkeypatching sleep/time and a fake transport so tests do not wait on real delays — covering: retry on 429 and 503, no retry on other 4xx/5xx, Retry-After honored for delta-seconds and HTTP-date, backoff growth and cap, stop at maximum attempts with the specified error, non-idempotent requests not retried, and explicit opt-in making them retryable. Keep all changes confined to the Python SDK client and its tests; do not add retry behavior to the server or the browser app, and do not modify contracts/retry-policy.md or clients/typescript. Run the unit tests you added and make them pass. Completion criterion: clients/python/client.py implements the contract, unit tests for the behaviors above exist in the Python test area, and the test run reports them passing.

nodes.name: conformance-review
nodes.task: Review the TypeScript and Python SDK retry implementations together for conformance to contracts/retry-policy.md, and record the outcome in tests/sdk-conformance.md (repository-relative paths; this is the repo root). The contract at contracts/retry-policy.md and both implementations (clients/typescript/client.ts, clients/python/client.py plus their unit tests) are present in your worktree. Compare the two clients clause by clause against the contract for the retryable status set (429/503), Retry-After parsing for both delta-seconds and HTTP-date including clamping and precedence over backoff, the exponential backoff formula with its base/multiplier/cap and jitter rule, the attempt limit default and config override naming, non-idempotent request protection including the safety signal and the default when absent, non-retryable status handling, transport-error handling, exhaustion behavior and the surfaced error shape, and confirm neither client introduced retry behavior into the server or browser app. Establish conformance empirically, not by reading code alone: for each policy clause write a reproducible scenario (given/when/then plus concrete inputs such as status sequence, Retry-After value, method/idempotence signal, configured max attempts), run the equivalent scenario against each client through its own unit-test harness with time/sleep and transport stubbed so the observed delay sequence and request attempt counts are directly comparable, and record the actual result for both clients side by side along with the exact commands used to reproduce them. tests/sdk-conformance.md must therefore contain the scenario set, the per-client observed outcomes, a clause-by-clause conformance table, and an overall verdict on whether the two clients use identical policy semantics. Treat any divergence between the clients, or any deviation of either client from the contract, as nonconformance. Completion criterion: tests/sdk-conformance.md exists with reproducible scenarios, recorded per-client results, a clause-by-clause comparison and a clear conformance verdict.

originalGoal: Add a consistent retry policy to the TypeScript and Python SDKs. Specify retryable HTTP statuses (429 and 503), Retry-After handling, exponential backoff, maximum attempts and non-idempotent request protection in a new contracts/retry-policy.md before implementation. Implement and unit-test that contract in clients/typescript/client.ts and clients/python/client.py. Review both clients together and write reproducible conformance scenarios and results in tests/sdk-conformance.md, checking both use identical policy semantics. If that review finds nonconformance, request corrections to both client implementations and repeat the conformance review. Do not put retry behavior in the server or browser app.
